toolArguments.prompt:
Use case: background-extraction. Convert ONLY the added flat-white contact paint in this ONE source image to a grayscale receiver mask. Output full1536x1024 opaque pure-black canvas, exact original coordinates.
There are FOUR intentional white-painted support shapes: under the skirt, under the side palm, under each of the two boot soles. Copy their exact locations and full shapes as WHITE cores. Keep actual toe-to-heel ground receiver directly BELOW the original boots, no shrink or move. Make only their outer edges gently taper through GRAY to BLACK over a SHORT6px source distance into immediately adjacent receiver, retaining the source-aligned white cores. The result is white contact cores and a modest soft gray skirt/hand/footprint edge, not an abrupt pure-white thin line and not a new oval shadow.
ALL other source RGB becomes solid BLACK, including all person/book/boots/metal highlights, naturally pale curtains/cushion/knit/lamp/furniture/floor. Do not trace any person contour, select natural white cloth, add far bench/floor or generate a room. Do not reinterpret where the boots stand; COPY THE WHITE PAINT COORDINATES from this input.
No crop, resize, shift, new pose, text, colors, labels, checkerboard or UI. It is a fixed-source luminance selection for original RGB once via MAX(F,S); no independent moving caster.
